title: model compatibility matrix and quant benchmark diary
summary: Experimental log combining a compact compatibility matrix with dated experiment entries for quantization formats, latency/throughput tradeoffs, and prompt pipeline adjustments for an enterprise POC (PHI-sensitive). Goal: pick a model+quant profile and a minimal pipeline that meets 200ms p95 for 32-token responses and keeps per-request cost under target while preserving QA metrics.
body:
Context:
- Customer: Acme Health (HIPAA scope). POC objective: 1) triage model candidates for on-prem/private deployment, 2) hit latency SLOs for short-answer flows (200ms p95 target for 32-token answers on dedicated A100 pool), 3) keep token-cost proxy under budget, 4) ensure logits fidelity for structured extraction tasks.

High-level approach:
- Build a simple compatibility matrix across model families and quant formats.
- Run short, reproducible microbenchmarks (generation latency, cold vs warm KV cache, and token throughput) plus a small evaluation set of domain prompts (10 canonical prompts + 5 extraction templates).
- Iterate prompt pipeline: system prompt tuning, instruction templates, prefix caching policy (reuse across related requests), and minibatching heuristics.

Compatibility matrix (quick conclusions):
- Llama2-13B: excellent cost/latency when int8/LLM.int8 conversion used; GPTQ int4 shows instability on structured extraction (drop in slot accuracy). Good for conversational and FAQ flows.
- MPT-30B: heavier memory; int8 quant reduces memory footprint but throughput still worse than Llama2-13B on same GPU. Robust on instruction-following; slightly higher latency.
- Falcon-40B: high raw quality for long-form but expensive; quant (bitsandbytes 8-bit) works but int4 not yet stable on our runtime kernels. Not recommended for 200ms SLO.
- RedCarve-7B (customer open-source specialized model we are evaluating): small, cheap; int4+KV cache gives excellent p95 but extraction accuracy lags on nested fields.

Quant formats tested and notes:
- GPTQ (4-bit): smallest memory but introduced hallucination/slot-shifts for extraction tasks in two seeds. Fastest in token/sec when KV cache hit rate high, but warmup variance high.
- bitsandbytes (8-bit): predictable latency, fewer regressions in accuracy, best stability for enterprise POC.
- LLMatrix/int8: good tradeoff; slightly higher memory than 4-bit but better accuracy for structured outputs.

Experiment diary (selected entries):
- 2024-01-18: baseline installs + dataset prep. Quick run: Llama2-13B bfloat16 on A100: cold p95 = 420ms for 32-token response; warm p95 = 180ms (KV caching works).
- 2024-01-20: convert Llama2-13B -> bitsandbytes 8-bit, same GPU pool: cold p95 = 260ms, warm p95 = 140ms. Extraction slot accuracy = 92% (baseline bfloat16 = 94%).
- 2024-01-22: GPTQ-4bit Llama2-13B: cold p95 = 210ms, warm p95 = 120ms. Extraction accuracy dropped to 82% and observed tokenization artifacts for some medical abbreviations. Repeatable across seeds.
- 2024-01-25: MPT-30B bitsandbytes: cold p95 = 520ms, warm p95 = 260ms. Extraction accuracy 95% but per-token cost 1.7x Llama2-13B int8.
- 2024-01-28: RedCarve-7B GPTQ-4bit with aggressive prefix cache: warm p95 = 85ms, but nested extraction F1 = 71% (poor).
- 2024-01-31: Prompt pipeline tweak: move heavy context into system prompt trimmed to 8 tokens of metadata; use template: "System: you are a medical summarizer for Acme Health. Extract fields: [A,B,C].
User: {case_notes}". Llama2-13B bitsandbytes warm p95 improved ~10ms due to shorter tokenization in pipeline. Extraction +1.5% absolute.

Prompt/pipeline experiments and heuristics discovered:
- System prompt brevity matters when tokenization of domain content is expensive. Small wins (5-15ms) on p95 by trimming redundant qualifiers.
- Prefix caching is highly effective: for multi-turn diagnostic dialogs where the same patient context repeats, reuse cached key-values for shared prefix (~30-40% p95 improvement). Important to bound cache size per-tenant.
- Minibatching: 8-request microbatch gave best GPU utilization without hurting p95 for short responses; above 16 saw p95 regressions due to enqueue delay.
- Deterministic extraction benefits from instruction templates that anchor markers (e.g., START_FIELD/END_FIELD) rather than free-text asks.

Quant/accuracy tradeoff table (verbal):
- bitsandbytes 8-bit: stable, small accuracy drop (~1–3%), deterministic behavior; best default for enterprise POC.
- GPTQ 4-bit: excellent throughput & memory; introduces correctness regressions for extraction on medical tokens; useful as a fallback for cheap inference when only conversational fidelity required.
- LLMatrix/int8 (our internal converter): middle ground, marginally higher latency than bnb but stronger extraction accuracy than GPTQ-4.

Anomalies and gotchas observed:
- Tokenization mismatch: some medical abbreviations tokenized into many small tokens on MPT variants causing latency spikes. Patch: pre-normalize abbreviations in preprocessor.
- Decoding differences: sampling temperature interactions with low-bit quant led to token degeneracy in one GPTQ seed (observed as repetition). Recommendation: keep temperature <=0.6 for GPTQ models on this workload.
- Cold-start penalty: first request after model load includes compilation (kernel selection) cost; warmup script with a 3-request synthetic warmup reduces this latency by ~40% for the first real request.

Decision (interim recommendation for POC):
- Primary candidate: Llama2-13B with bitsandbytes 8-bit quant on dedicated A100 pool. Rationale: meets latency SLO (warm p95 ≈140ms), good extraction accuracy (~92%), stable behavior, smaller operational risk than GPTQ.
- Fallback route: GPTQ-4bit Llama2-13B for best-cost mode only on non-extraction, conversational endpoints. Put a routing policy to avoid GPTQ variant for extraction-intent requests.
- For extremely latency-sensitive short primitives (under 100ms), consider RedCarve-7B int4 but only for fixed-output templates (not nested extraction).

Operational checklist for next cycle:
- Confirm KMS/HSM integrations for Acme Health private deployment (security gating).
- Implement warmup hook in deployment manifest to run 3 synthetic prompts after model load.
- Add prompt preprocessor to normalize abbreviations and strip non-essential metadata.
- Instrument fine-grained KV-cache hit telemetry in the console for this deployment route.
- Add a canary routing policy: 80% traffic to bitsandbytes Llama2-13B, 20% to bfloat16 baseline for comparison during week 1.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Should we try a hybrid cascade: RedCarve-7B for short autoreplies and Llama2-13B-bnb for complex extracts? Need to prototype cascade glue and latency overhead.
- How much per-tenant KV cache memory should we reserve to prevent eviction-induced regressions? (initial conservative cap: 2GB/tenant).
- Customer legal: validate if 8-bit quantization is acceptable under their encryption/processing policy.

Metrics to collect during POC (tracked in the PRD dashboard):
- p95 latency (cold and warm windows separated), mean latency, throughput tokens/sec, KV-cache hit ratio, extraction F1/slot accuracy, per-request cost estimate, memory consumption per model instance, error/rejection rates.

Next steps (owners & timeline):
- Week 1 (Ethan): deploy bitsandbytes Llama2-13B private cluster + warmup hook, add telemetry (due 2024-02-07).
- Week 1 (Lina): implement preprocessor normalization and template anchor enforcement + regression tests (due 2024-02-09).
- Week 2 (Noah & Priya): run canary 80/20, collect metrics for 3 business days, produce go/no-go recommendation (due 2024-02-16).

Appendix: reproducible commands (notes)
- Convert to bnb: 
  python scripts/convert_to_bnb.py --model llama-13b --out /models/llama-13b-bnb --optimize-kv
- Run microbenchmark: 
  ./bench/run_gen.sh --model /models/llama-13b-bnb --gpu a100 --batch 8 --seq 256 --num_requests 500
- Warmup hook example (manifest snippet): 
  postLoad: [
    {cmd: "generate --model /models/llama-13b-bnb --prompt 'warmup' --max_tokens 32"}
  ]

Notes to self: keep these diary entries chronological and snapshot raw logs into the Confluence page linked above. If we decide to try GPTQ again, run extraction-focused token-level debug traces to pinpoint token shifts.

End of diary entry.
